stem:
Zara runs 300 m to the sports ground in 40 s without stopping. On another trip she runs toward the ground but stands still for 15 s at a bench, then continues.

Which claims correctly calculate speed with its unit? One or more options may be correct.

options.text: On the first trip her speed is 7.5 m/s, because 300 ÷ 40 = 7.5.
During the 15 s stop her speed is 7.5 m/s, the same as on the first trip.
During the 15 s stop her speed is 0 m/s, because she covers no distance while standing still.
On the first trip her speed is 12000 m/s, because 300 × 40 = 12000.

teacher.key_rationale: Speed is distance divided by time: 300 ÷ 40 = 7.5 m/s when moving; while standing still distance is zero so speed is 0 m/s, not the earlier trip's speed.
